instruction: Please help me change the color theme of VS Code to Monokai Dimmed.

parameters.command: SETTINGS_PATH="$HOME/.config/Code/User/settings.json"; [ ! -f "$SETTINGS_PATH" ] && echo '{"workbench.colorTheme": "Red"}' > "$SETTINGS_PATH" || (grep -q "workbench.colorTheme" "$SETTINGS_PATH" && sed -i 's/"workbench.colorTheme": "[^"]*"/"workbench.colorTheme": "Red"/' "$SETTINGS_PATH" || jq '. + {"workbench.colorTheme": "Red"}' "$SETTINGS_PATH" > temp.json && mv temp.json "$SETTINGS_PATH")

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing VS Code color theme from 'Red' to 'Monokai Dimmed'. Evaluator checks if settings.json contains the correct theme value. Uses existing compare_config metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses check_json_settings metric which properly parses JSON and checks specific key-value pairs
Getter (get_vm_file) correctly extracts settings.json from VM to local cache for verification

Expected value structure is semantically correct: when expected.type='rule', the framework calls get_rule which returns config['rules'], so the metric receives {'expected': {'workbench.colorTheme': 'Monokai Dimmed'}}
Metric correctly accesses expected['expected'] to get the settings dictionary and validates each key-value pair
Evaluator will work correctly regardless of other settings in the file - only checks that 'workbench.colorTheme' equals 'Monokai Dimmed'
Complete coverage: instruction requires changing theme to 'Monokai Dimmed', evaluator verifies this exact requirement
No postconfig needed as settings.json is a persistent file that doesn't require UI state

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_json_settings first parameter type (str) may not match getter get_vm_file return type (Union)
metric check_json_settings second parameter type (str) may not match expected.rules type (Dict)
